content: The use of ramipril should not significantly affect minimum phenprocoumon levels or interfere with the patient’s anticoagulation status. In rare cases where no suitable alternative exists for a patient requiring therapy with drugs that affect the renin-angiotensin system, the mother should be informed of the potential risks to the fetus. Serial ultrasound examinations should be performed to monitor the intra-amniotic environment. If oligohydramnios is detected, discontinue Altace unless it is deemed life-saving for the mother. Fetal testing may be appropriate depending on the gestational age. However, it is important to note that oligohydramnios may not manifest until after irreversible fetal injury has occurred. Infants with a history of in utero exposure to Altace should be closely monitored for hypotension, oliguria, and hyperkalemia. A pharmacokinetic study conducted in hospitalized elderly patients demonstrated that peak plasma levels of ramiprilat and the area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC) for ramiprilat are higher in older individuals. A single-dose pharmacokinetic study was conducted in hypertensive patients with varying degrees of renal impairment who received a single 10 mg dose of ramipril. Patients were categorized into four groups based on their initial creatinine clearance estimates: normal renal function (>80 mL/min), mild impairment (40–80 mL/min), moderate impairment (15–40 mL/min), and severe impairment (<15 mL/min). The plasma levels of ramiprilat were approximately twofold higher in patients with mild, moderate, and severe renal impairment compared to those with normal renal function. These findings suggest that the starting dose of ramipril should be reduced in patients with moderate-to-severe renal impairment. Altace capsules should generally be swallowed whole. However, the capsules can be opened, and their contents sprinkled on approximately 4 ounces of applesauce or mixed with 4 ounces (120 mL) of water or apple juice. To ensure the full dose of ramipril is consumed, the entire mixture should be ingested. These mixtures can be prepared in advance and stored for up to 24 hours at room temperature or up to 48 hours under refrigeration. Concomitant administration of Altace with potassium supplements, potassium salt substitutes, or potassium-sparing diuretics can lead to increased serum potassium levels. Laboratory determinations of serum levels of ramipril and its metabolites are not widely available and have no established role in managing ramipril overdose. There is no evidence that altering urine pH or other measures can accelerate the elimination of ramipril and its metabolites. Similarly, it is unclear whether any of these substances can be effectively removed from the body via hemodialysis. Angiotensin II could theoretically serve as a specific antagonist or antidote in cases of ramipril overdose, but it is largely unavailable outside of specialized research facilities. Since the hypotensive effect of ramipril is achieved through vasodilation and effective hypovolemia, treatment of ramipril overdose may involve the infusion of normal saline solution. The antihypertensive effect of ramipril appears to result, at least in part, from the inhibition of both tissue and circulating angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) activity, thereby reducing the formation of angiotensin II in both tissue and plasma.
